title: XLOOKUP with a fallback when nothing matches

screens.prompt: In B6, look up the price of the SKU in B5, and return "not stocked" when the list has no such SKU.

hints.syntax: =XLOOKUP(B5,A2:A4,B2:B4,"not stocked"): the fourth slot is the text for a miss.
hints.func-xlookup: Four arguments here. The fourth only matters when nothing matches, and the three-argument form would show #N/A.
hints.require-ref: Search for the SKU in B5, so asking about another one is a single edit.
hints.value: TX-104 is not in the list, so the answer is the fallback, spelled as the prompt spells it.
hints.error: The search column and the return column must match in size: three SKUs against three prices, or #VALUE!.

reject.why: the closing bracket is missing, so nothing runs
VLOOKUP has no fallback argument, so a missed SKU comes back as #N/A with no words around it
the three-argument form has no fallback, so this returns #N/A instead of a sentence
the fallback is shown exactly as typed, and a capital N is a different answer from the one asked for
the SKU typed into the formula, so changing the asked-for SKU means editing the formula
the search column is four cells deep and the return column is three, so the sizes do not agree

docs.explain:
The list holds three SKUs and B5 asks for TX-104, which is not among them. A three-argument XLOOKUP would answer #N/A, and a column of #N/A sends the reader to the formula bar to work out what went wrong.

The fourth argument is the text to show instead. XLOOKUP returns "not stocked" and the cell reads as a sentence. That text appears exactly as typed, so the lower case in the prompt is part of the answer.

Use it on sheets that other people read. The fallback should say what is missing, and it should never be a zero, because a zero passes for a price.

errors.text: No fallback was supplied, so a SKU that is not in A2:A4 came back with nothing to say.
The search column and the return column are different sizes, and some rows have no partner.

docs.atWork: A stock sheet where a discontinued SKU has to read as out of stock in an email, rather than #N/A.
docs.outcome: Answer a missing SKU with a sentence instead of an error.

seo.title: XLOOKUP fallback in Excel: no #N/A
seo.description: The fourth argument replaces #N/A with text a reader can follow. B5 asks for TX-104, so the cell says not stocked while listed SKUs still return prices.
